text: {"frames":["Dirk lunges at the gilt frame just as the lady in the painting lifts her hand off her lap. She has sat still for three hundred years, and tonight she is leaning toward the stairs as if she wants to leave. The dream seller at the next stall swears the paint was always like that, but Dirk saw her sleeve move. He presses the canvas flat, and her hand goes still, yet the clock beside her has its hands set at a time nobody ever chose. What time does the clock in the picture show, written with digits?","Imogen wants her barge through the lock before the ice closes the canal, and she wants it badly enough to shout at the water. The water in the lock sinks, rises, sinks again, slow as breathing. Her apprentice Joost says the gate is sulking because nobody has greased its hinges. They argue over the rope while the barge bumps the wall and the lock keeper's clock ticks above the door. What time does the clock in the picture show, written with digits?","Smells of hot waffles and wet wool drift down a staircase that is not on the plan. Sander the mapmaker says the floor does not exist, and Lotte the cheese maker says it does and bets him a wheel of cheese. They climb together, counting steps under their breath, and the air gets warmer with every turn. At the top a door stands ajar, and a windmill clock is ticking on the other side. What time does the clock in the picture show, written with digits?","A blue lantern bobs across the barge, and nobody is holding it. Fenna the learned owl blinks at it from the mast, then rustles down with a plan in her beak. She sets a trail of cheese rinds across the deck so the lantern will follow it to the mill. The lantern floats after the rinds, and a clock on the mill wall begins to chime its hour. What time does the clock in the picture show, written with digits?","The canal flows uphill toward the windmill, and Briony the stork is wading the wrong way. Every boat in Misty Ford sails backwards on the night tide, and the rule is old and kindly meant. Briony tells the captain to wait for the water to turn, and the boats creak against their moorings. A small clock hangs above the sluice, its hands moving backwards with the water. What time does the clock in the picture show, written with digits?"]}
